Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for agreeing to evaluate this 8-year-old boy. His bone fragility has been an ongoing concern essentially since birth, with manifestations noted from the neonatal period onward. 

He recently presented following a simple fall from standing height that resulted in an acute, minimally displaced fracture of his left elbow. This represents his fourth skeletal break over the past three years, each following minimal mechanical force. A recent bone densitometry study confirmed significantly compromised mineralization, with a lumbar spine Z-score of -2.8. In addition, his linear growth has been severely attenuated, with his standing height persistently charting below the first percentile. On examination, a prominent slate-blue hue of his sclerae was readily visible. 

The remainder of his physical evaluation was non-contributory. He has supple extremities with full range of motion throughout and no joint contractures. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no evidence of an enlarged liver or spleen. He is doing well socially, attends regular third-grade classes, and displays completely age-appropriate development without any cognitive deficits. A formal hearing screen was completed last month and confirmed normal auditory function bilaterally. Basic laboratory investigations, including a comprehensive metabolic panel and circulating alkaline phosphatase levels, were all within normal reference ranges, showing no elevated enzyme values. 

He currently takes an over-the-counter vitamin D supplement. Both parents and his younger brother are healthy, with no significant family medical history. 

I would greatly appreciate your assessment regarding his recurrent skeletal trauma and low bone mass, as well as your recommendations for further diagnostic evaluation. 

Sincerely, 
Dr. Marcus Vance
